script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Calling this Paul's whole job description claims a completeness the verse does not state.
The cookie comparison doesn't click: holding a promise is not the same action as holding a cookie, so the punchline is muddled.
Saying this is the part Paul wants the baker to lean on assigns him an unstated intention.
The command came from God, but the text doesn't say the proclamation was not Paul's own idea or that it didn't come from a committee.
The claim about Peter covers the entire letter, and Peter's identity as an apostle comes from outside this passage. Neither has an applicable reference.
The explanation merely substitutes elders for judges and repeats the answer. It is flat and adds no useful explanation.
Referring to the rest of the stop exposes the lesson's structure to the baker.

Calling it the opposite of hiding the teaching from outsiders implies the text says it is shared with outsiders. It says the overseer can encourage others and refute those who contradict it, without identifying those people as outsiders.
The explanation quotes the answer and then comments that it is a strong word. It is generic and doesn't explain the situation.
Silencing the teachers is not necessarily the opposite of welcoming them as people. Paul does not say they must not be welcomed.
The explanation only quotes the answer and repeats that revenge is not mentioned. It is flat and offers no further explanation.
The sticky-note comparison contrasts a method with the sternness of a rebuke. A rebuke on a sticky note could still be stern, so the joke doesn't follow.
The explanation quotes the answer and repeats that sending them away is not mentioned. It is generic and adds no explanation.
No waiting around adds urgency or timing that Paul does not state.
Staying sound implies they are already sound in the faith. Paul states the goal as their becoming sound.
The passage does not say the myths sound good or describe them as a pile of tall tales.
Saying prophets show up in verse 12 suggests more than one; Paul quotes one of their own prophets.
